A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching SPLICE to its renamed counterpart SPLINCE.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, language-model intervention and CelebA image experiments, with additional empirical analyses in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds vision classification, OOD-method comparisons, and Mistral and Phi-2 evaluations.

M1.justification: The optimization objective, kernel and covariance-preservation constraints, closed-form projection in Equation 4, and mean correction remain unchanged. Renaming SPLICE to SPLINCE and evaluating additional models do not alter the proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix B.5 adds Waterbirds classification while removing background information and extends CelebA from qualitative pixel interventions to quantitative glasses classification under varying smile–glasses associations. Existing NLP datasets and tasks remain.

E2.justification: Figures 13–14 add training-set deep feature reweighting (DFRTR) and last-layer group distributionally robust optimization (GDRO) as evaluated comparators on vision and NLP classification tasks. The original ERM/original-model, SAL and LEACE comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: New protocols include Waterbirds train/validation/test sizes of 4,775/1,199/5,796, ResNet50 fine-tuning for 100 epochs, and CelebA logistic regression. Appendix B.6 adds Mistral 7B v0.3 and Phi-2 configurations on existing language tasks. These extend the evaluation settings without replacing the original protocols.

E4.justification: Appendix B.5 substantially extends robustness testing through task–concept correlation sweeps on vision data, exposing deteriorating performance under stronger spurious associations and comparing resilience against OOD methods. The existing regularization, covariance-preservation, image-difference and multilayer analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: The added NLP comparison in Figure 14 reports five seeds for both datasets, whereas the retained Figure 2 specifies three for Bias in Bios and five for detoxification. This adds a different reported replication count for the new comparison, without establishing that the original experiment was rerun. Existing confidence-interval and significance-testing practices remain.

E6.justification: Figures 12–15 and Table 5 add substantial results, including weaker vision performance relative to DFRTR/GDRO and mixed outcomes on additional LMs. For Mistral, Table 5 reports exp(beta_fact) of 14.76 for SPLINCE versus 10.00 for LEACE. Original matched results, including Table 1 and the full Bias in Bios table renumbered from 5 to 6, are retained.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.3 introduces excess-risk definitions, Theorems 3–4 and their proofs for frozen linear and logistic predictors, claiming zero excess risk for SPLINCE under specified assumptions. This substantially extends the theory beyond the retained projection and retraining-equivalence results.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims of linear concept removal with target-covariance preservation, minimum distortion under those constraints, and empirical benefits on NLP tasks. Renaming and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these main contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive discussion of poorer vision performance, fairness guarantees versus OOD generalization, possible small-sample overfitting by the new comparators, and Phi-2's weak task performance. It also qualifies the new theoretical assumptions, identifies possible cross-modal covariance misalignment, and adds explicit linear-only fairness and deployment limitations in Appendix D.

D1.justification: v2 adds a link to experimental code and the SPLINCE implementation. Appendices C.1–C.2 document Waterbirds construction and splits, ResNet50 optimization settings, DFRTR group balancing and GDRO's update rate. Existing BERT, E5 and Llama settings are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused references for DFR, additional language models, Waterbirds source datasets and CLIP, and distinguishes concept-removal fairness from OOD generalization. The core positioning relative to LEACE and other concept-erasure methods remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The method is renamed throughout, wording and header details are corrected, and explanatory paragraphs and appendix subsections are added. The main section order and most existing prose remain intact; there is no extensive narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds four figures, Figures 12–15, and a new Table 5 covering the expanded comparisons. It also updates plot labels, relocates retained figures and tables, and corrects Figure 6's comparator name from LEACE to SAL. The former full Bias in Bios Table 5 is retained as Table 6.

improvement.justification: The broader comparisons, reported vision failures and code link improve empirical coverage and transparency. However, new Appendix A.3 introduces theoretical problems: Theorem 3 treats P beta = beta as also implying P^T beta = beta for an oblique projector, while Theorem 4's final cancellation does not follow from Equation 44 for general covariance. These unsupported guarantees coexist with meaningful empirical gains, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
